To find the remainder when the 100th term of the Fibonacci sequence is divided by 8, we use the concept of the Pisano period. The Pisano period for modulo 8 is the period with which the sequence of Fibonacci numbers taken modulo 8 repeats.

We list the Fibonacci numbers modulo 8 to find the repeating cycle:

\[
\begin{align*}
\text{Term 1:} & \quad 1 \mod 8 = 1 \\
\text{Term 2:} & \quad 1 \mod 8 = 1 \\
\text{Term 3:} & \quad (1 + 1) \mod 8 = 2 \\
\text{Term 4:} & \quad (1 + 2) \mod 8 = 3 \\
\text{Term 5:} & \quad (2 + 3) \mod 8 = 5 \\
\text{Term 6:} & \quad (3 + 5) \mod 8 = 0 \\
\text{Term 7:} & \quad (5 + 0) \mod 8 = 5 \\
\text{Term 8:} & \quad (0 + 5) \mod 8 = 5 \\
\text{Term 9:} & \quad (5 + 5) \mod 8 = 10 \mod 8 = 2 \\
\text{Term 10:} & \quad (5 + 2) \mod 8 = 7 \\
\text{Term 11:} & \quad (2 + 7) \mod 8 = 9 \mod 8 = 1 \\
\text{Term 12:} & \quad (7 + 1) \mod 8 = 0 \\
\text{Term 13:} & \quad (1 + 0) \mod 8 = 1 \\
\text{Term 14:} & \quad (0 + 1) \mod 8 = 1 \\
\end{align*}
\]

We observe that the sequence repeats every 12 terms starting from Term 1. Therefore, the Pisano period for modulo 8 is 12. To find the remainder of the 100th term, we compute:

\[
100 \mod 12 = 4
\]

This means the remainder when the 100th term is divided by 8 is the same as the remainder when the 4th term is divided by 8. The 4th term in the Fibonacci sequence is 3. Therefore, the remainder is:

\[
3 \mod 8 = 3
\]

Thus, the remainder when the 100th term of the Fibonacci sequence is divided by 8 is \(\boxed{3}\).
